annotation.authors_or_issuer: 内閣府・国土交通省 (Cabinet Office and Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism)
key_provisions_or_claims: Classifies road signs into main signs (guide, warning, regulatory, instruction) and auxiliary signs, and sets their types, placement and designs in appended tables.
Specifies lane markings and road markings, and when lane lines count as road markings under the Road Traffic Act.
Allocates sign installation between road administrators and prefectural public safety commissions.
Includes 'remotely operated small vehicles' (delivery robots) alongside pedestrians as 'pedestrians etc.' for traffic rules and signs.
The June 2026 amendment takes effect on 1 September 2026 and carries transitional provisions for maximum-speed signs and markings.
annotation.summary_en: Japan's ministerial ordinance on road signs, lane lines and road markings (Showa 35, No. 3), shown in the revision effective 1 September 2026. It standardises the types, placement and design of traffic signs and markings. Its signs now cover pedestrians and remotely operated small vehicles (delivery robots), but robotics is only a marginal theme.
